Putin adviser Aleksandr Dugin: Baudet is a ticket for the future

Aleksandr Dugin, the ultra-reactionary Russian thinker Aleksandr Dugin is 'very charmed' by FvD leader Thierry Baudet after a meeting last year. According to him, his electorial victory shows that major change is imminent in the West.

by Steven Derix, March 24, 2019 at 11:37

 

Aleksandr Dugin heard the news about Thierry Baudet's monster victory in the Provincial State elections with "great joy and enthusiasm," the Russian ultra-conservative thinker says on the phone in Moscow. Dugin (57) speaks lyrically about the leader of the Forum for Democracy. "One of the most intellectual thinkers I have ever met. A completely original and independent man. A rising star."

Baudet and Dugin have known each other since last year. On April 7, the Russian gave a lecture during a philosophical congress in the Westerkerk in Amsterdam. Fifteen minutes before the event started, Thierry Baudet slipped in. After the meeting, Baudet addressed the Russian.

The next day the two men met again, and now they talked for hours: about the EU, but also about the history of the Reformation and the influence of Celtic-Roman and Germanic culture. Baudet was well acquainted with Dugin's ideas about the imminent end of liberalism, and the "fourth political theory" - the ideology, that comes after communism, fascism and liberalism.

The Russian thinker was immediately charmed by the 36-year-old member of parliament. "He has a fantastic style, very classical, very attractive. I love the dandyism of Thierry Baudet. "

 

Popular with European populists

Since the annexation of Crimea and the confrontation between Russia and the West, the ultra-reactionary ideas of Aleksandr Gelyevich Dugin have become well-studied. Western media call him 'Putin's advisor'. Dugin is popular among populists in Europe for his ruthless criticism of liberal society, with its 'exaggerated' attention to equal rights, gender politics and individual self-development.

According to Dugin, liberalism is at the edge of the abyss - an idea that is similar to Baudet's picture of the decline of Western civilization. "We have long and substantively talked about what would happen if people with views like me and him had the power in the Netherlands," says Dugin. "We agreed that the Dutch national identity must be strengthened." (Also read this earlier interview with Aleksandr Dugin : "When I had completely mastered fascism, I came to a total rejection of racism and nationalism.")

Not that the two men agreed on everything. The Russian thinker is not a supporter of the nation state, such as Baudet, and is not an opponent of the EU ("I think Europe must be one").

Despite his many years of flirting with fascist thinkers, Dugin says he loathes racism. In an interview with NRC , he spoke out late about Geert Wilders. But Baudet is not tainted by xenophobia, says Dugin: “He is opposed to migration and the spread of Islam, but that applies to a significant part of European society. But I didn't notice any xenophobia in him. "\

 

"Do not instantly demonize"

Politicians such as Baudet meet a social demand, says Dugin. "A question to which the liberal globalist discourse has no answer at all." According to him, the victory of the Forum for Democracy last week shows once again that a fundamental change is on the way in Western society.

Dugin often compares the West with the Soviet Union at the end of the 1980s. "The West is, I have no doubt about this, on the verge of ending the liberal paradigm. Nobody knows what will replace it. Neither does Baudet. But he understands that there must be alternatives. In that regard, Baudet is a ticket for the future."

Dugin dismisses comments such as 'fascism has won in the Netherlands'. "Someone who does not agree with liberalism is not immediately a fascist. Instead of demonizing it is better to have a quiet intellectual conversation about the future ahead."

And what about the word "boreal," which Baudet used again in his victory speech last Wednesday? Dugin, scornfully: "Boreal simply means 'northern': Northern Europe. To immediately see some sort of racism in there is just ridiculous. Paranoid."

With some raising of votes: "How much can a person tolerate? The Dutch have chosen an interesting curious politician. Why curse him immediately because he said a certain word? It is laughable!
